verdictSummary: Every measurement the C3 record makes is accurate and I reproduced all of them, most beyond their recorded sample sizes (41/41 + 37/37 digests against disk AND the 4d431ce objects; 13/13 required selectors; 93/93 evidence selectors; 32/32 selector digests, not the recorded 6-sample; 6/6 executions with both EP13 stdout digests byte-exact; 12/12 resolvable derivations at 0 errors under my own resolver AND the corpus resolver, canonicals 872883db and 4241f87b reproduced under both; the retention terminus form judged LAWFUL). The manifests' own sentences are honest. But DR-001's criterion cannot be discharged vacuously this time: my recompute finds live conflicts with no recorded design delta -- including a NEW third instance of the DR204-F5 claim-register defect class (R-1 binds the v1.6 name to v1.5's digest) that the regenerated baseline re-pinned, which the baseline's own stop-on-conflict rule forbids -- and DR-204 requirement 1 is only half-executed (applied heads added; their standing evidence pinned in neither manifest; matrix rows not regenerated). A SATISFIED re-record today would repeat the provenance pattern DR-204 just ruled unlawful: a grade whose own definition is not met at recording time.

findings.finding: NEW claim-register conflict, third instance of the DR204-F5 class, missed by both the DR-204 audit and the C-D004 repair: claim R-1 binds bindingArtifact 'artifacts/r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.6.json' to bindingArtifactSha256 557b9f973c22b7ea959a884f56d5bac81c5383e227cac73a47605c1be317a815 -- which is EXACTLY the digest of r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.5.json. The v1.6 file has had exactly one committed digest in its entire history (created at 4d201a3): 14c46b6582b573c1ac253d891e4813bcc436117adacaa5fc74ede0ab5ae23d3c, which is what the baseline and the matrix both correctly pin. The register's R-1 note ('The binding is now v1.5'), bindingArtifactReview (the v1.5 prefreeze review, a0dd24a5...), and currentReviewArtifacts all still describe v1.5: the filename was repointed to v1.6 without moving the digest, review, or narrative -- the same v11-name/v9-digest pattern DR204-F5 found on C-2. Consequence: the regenerated baseline re-pins register bytes carrying a binding digest that matches no committed bytes of the named file, and the authorityRule's 'Stop on any mismatch or conflict' halts R-1 claim-status resolution. Sweep context: of the register's 18 digest-bearing binding/review citations, this is the only mismatch.
